# Does a calibration carry across recordings? (generated by scripts/calibration.py --part transfer)

Test data: the late part of each person's music record only. Calibration: the first 30 s of the music record (same record as the test data, ~35 min earlier) or of the after-music record (a separate recording, made after the music record). U-Net rows: 3 seeds, averaged per person.

## Means over the 16 development people

|:---------------------------------------|------:|-------:|----------:|-----------:|------------------:|------------:|-------------:|---------:|--------------:|
| ('avg_beat_own', 'after_music_start')  | 0.875 |  0.478 |     0.994 |      0.975 |             3.188 |       5.417 |        0.963 |    0.963 |         0.977 |
| ('avg_beat_own', 'music_start')        | 0.904 |  0.429 |     0.991 |      0.965 |             2.625 |       3.07  |        0.966 |    0.97  |         0.992 |
| ('unet', 'none')                       | 0.613 |  0.798 |     0.972 |      0.931 |            12.458 |      10.501 |        0.651 |    0.618 |         1.059 |

## Same record vs other record, person by person

- unet_shift: calibrating on the other record instead of the same one changes r by +0.022 on average (lower for 5 of 16 people; Wilcoxon p = 0.0691)
- unet_finetune: calibrating on the other record instead of the same one changes r by +0.010 on average (lower for 5 of 16 people; Wilcoxon p = 0.0214)
- avg_beat_own: calibrating on the other record instead of the same one changes r by -0.029 on average (lower for 9 of 16 people; Wilcoxon p = 0.528)
